_groups.name: Form
_groups.description: How a song is sung in the roda, from the opening litany to the call and response.

_groups.name: Toque
_groups.description: The berimbau rhythm, and the style of game that rhythm asks for.

_groups.name: The game
_groups.description: The circle, the bow, the step, and the trick.

_groups.name: People
_groups.description: Mestres and other figures the songs call by name.

_groups.name: History
_groups.description: Slavery, the quilombos, and the word liberdade.

_groups.name: Place
_groups.description: Bahia, the sea, Africa, and the other places the songs keep in view.

_groups.name: Daily life
_groups.description: Work, money, friendship, longing, and the day around the game.

_groups.name: Related arts
_groups.description: Dances and musics taught beside capoeira.

_groups.name: Recordings
_groups.description: Albums and repertoire sets these songs were taken from.

aberre.description: Songs that name Mestre Aberrê, an Angola mestre the repertoire often sets beside Pastinha, Waldemar, and Traíra.

afoxe.description: Afoxé is carnival street music from Bahia with a candomblé ijexá beat. Some capoeira groups bring these songs into demonstrations and the roda.

africa.description: Songs that remember Africa as origin, ancestry, and return — the root many lyrics name when they talk about where capoeira comes from.

amazonas.description: Songs that name Amazonas, the river and the state, as a place in the repertoire.

amizade.description: Songs about friendship, and how rare a straight friend is inside the game.

angola.description: Capoeira Angola is the older, closer game: played low and slow, with a strong ritual around the berimbau. The ladainha and chula belong to this circle.

areia.description: Songs of the sand. Some are the work corrido about gathering it (“Vamos apanhar areia”); others put the beach, or a grain of sand, in the title.

axe.description: Axé is life force and blessing, a word from candomblé that the roda uses when the energy is high.

axe-capoeira-vol-1.description: First Axé Capoeira album with Mestre Barrão.

axe-capoeira-vol-2.description: Second Axé Capoeira album with Mestre Barrão.

axe-capoeira-vol-3.description: Third Axé Capoeira album with Mestre Barrão.

axe-capoeira-vol-4.description: Fourth Axé Capoeira album with Mestre Barrão.

bahia.description: Songs that keep Bahia in the title, or come back to the name line after line.

barrao.description: Songs associated with Mestre Barrão and the Axé Capoeira repertoire.

benguela.description: Benguela is a mid-tempo toque and game, between Angola and São Bento Grande: grounded, tricky, and less of a fight than the fast games.

berimbau.description: Songs about the berimbau, the musical bow that leads the roda: its toques, its voice, and the respect due to it.

besouro.description: Songs about Besouro Mangangá of Santo Amaro, the capoeirista whose fights turned into legend.

bimba.description: Songs that name Mestre Bimba (Manoel dos Reis Machado), the teacher who shaped Capoeira Regional in Salvador.

boi.description: Songs of the ox: the vaqueiro, the bumba meu boi, and the animal that does not come back from the woods.

canjiquinha.description: Songs that name Mestre Canjiquinha, a singer and Angola mestre from Bahia.

capoeira.description: Songs that speak of capoeira itself — what it is, who plays, and why it matters — rather than a side story in the lyric.

cavalaria.description: Cavalaria is a warning toque. It once told the roda that police or outsiders were coming, so the game could change or stop.

chula.description: In Capoeira Angola, the chula is the praise song after the ladainha. Players stay at the foot of the berimbau; the game begins when it finishes.

cobra.description: Songs in which the cobra is a figure — the bite, the hole, the coral snake — rather than a passing comparison.

corrido.description: Corridos are call-and-response songs sung while the game is on. The soloist calls a line and the chorus answers, keeping the roda moving.

culture.description: Songs about custom and everyday Bahia around the roda: food, feast days, and the life beside the game.

dende.description: Dendê is palm oil. In the roda the word means the game has flavor and force.

dinheiro.description: Songs about money — who has it, who lost it, and what it cannot buy.

escravidao.description: Songs of slavery: the senzala, the overseer, the whip, and what stayed after abolition.

folklore.description: Folk themes that sit next to the fight: animals, work, and feast-day stories sung in the round.

ginga.description: Songs about the ginga, the swaying base step of capoeira, and the malícia inside that movement.

history.description: Songs that tell capoeira’s past: quilombos, persecution, revolt, and mestres who kept the game alive.

idalina.description: Traditional corridos that call Idalina — and sometimes Catarina — into the game.

instruments.description: Songs that name the orchestra of the roda: berimbau, pandeiro, atabaque, agogô, and reco-reco.

iuna.description: Iúna is a solemn toque reserved for high-graduation games and demonstrations, usually without the usual call-and-response singing.

joao-grande.description: Songs that name Mestre João Grande, the Angola mestre who learned from João Pequeno.

joao-pequeno.description: Songs that name Mestre João Pequeno, the Angola teacher linked with Pastinha.

jogo-de-dentro.description: Jogo de dentro is the close game, played where there is no room to run. These songs name it.

ladainha.description: The ladainha is the opening litany of a Capoeira Angola roda. One voice sings a story or prayer while the circle listens; the game does not start until it ends.

legends.description: Story songs of the game: Besouro, Saci, and other folk figures whose names still get called in the roda.

liberdade.description: Songs that speak of liberdade, freedom itself. The Liberdade neighborhood in Salvador, and the epithet in “Waldemar da Liberdade,” are not this tag.

louvacao.description: Songs of praise (louvação), often for mestres, orixás, or capoeira itself, sung before the game opens.

maculele.description: Maculelê is a stick dance from Bahia, often taught alongside capoeira. These songs belong to that game, not to the roda proper.

malicia.description: Songs about malícia: showing less than you know, and letting the other player step into the trap.

mandinga.description: Songs about mandinga: the cunning, almost magical side of capoeira — feints, charm, and not showing everything you know.

mar.description: Songs of the sea: the tide, the shore, the sailor, and the crossing.

menino.description: Songs with menino or menina in the title: the boy or the girl the verse is spoken to.

mestres.description: Songs that name teachers and lineage: who taught whom, and who is owed respect in the roda.

mestres-boca-rica-e-bigodinho-capoeira-a.description: Capoeira Angola recording by Mestres Boca Rica and Bigodinho.

mulher.description: Songs about women. A title that calls her morena, iaiá, or sinhá is included; a stray “ô iaiá” at the end of a line is not.

nago.description: Songs that name nagô, the Yoruba nation in Bahia, as a lineage of capoeira or as a people.

navalha.description: Songs of the navalha and the sharpened knife, the blade the old game remembers.

orixa.description: Songs that greet or tell of the orixás of candomblé, whose stories sit under much of the ritual around the roda.

parana.description: Paraná is the answer shouted back in a famous corrido. These are the songs that carry that call in the title, not the state and not Mestre Paraná.

pastinha.description: Songs that name Mestre Pastinha (Vicente Ferreira Pastinha), the teacher most tied to Capoeira Angola in the twentieth century.

places.description: Songs that name Bahia, Salvador, the sea, or other places the repertoire keeps coming back to.

quadra.description: Quadras are short four-line verses. They often sit between the ladainha and the corridos, or stand as compact songs of their own.

quilombo.description: Songs of the quilombo and of Palmares, the communities built by people who had escaped slavery.

regional.description: Capoeira Regional is the style created by Mestre Bimba: a faster, more upright game with its own sequence of lessons and songs.

religion.description: Songs with prayer, saints, orixás, or the church — the spiritual layer of the repertoire.

revelacao-de-liminha.description: Revelação de Liminha, a named recording in the collection.

roda.description: Songs about the circle itself: who enters, who watches, and how the game is offered at the foot of the berimbau.

saci.description: Songs of Saci-Pererê, the one-legged trickster of Brazilian folklore.

salvador.description: Songs that name Salvador, the city of the roda. “São Salvador” is included.

samba-de-roda.description: Samba de roda from Recôncavo Baiano, a close cousin of capoeira: clapping, atabaque, and a singer in the round.

santa-maria.description: Santa Maria is the toque Mestre Bimba treated as the hymn of Capoeira Regional. These songs name it.

sao-bento-grande.description: São Bento Grande is a fast toque for an open, upright game — the classic Regional rhythm for kicks and escapes.

sao-bento-pequeno.description: São Bento Pequeno is a quicker Angola toque, still close to the ground but livelier than the slow Angola game.

saudade.description: Songs of saudade: longing for a person, a place, or a time that does not come back.

sereia.description: Songs of the sereia, the mermaid who shows up in stories beside the roda.

suassuna.description: Songs that name Mestre Suassuna in the lyric. A title that only credits him as the author is not enough.

traira.description: Songs that name Mestre Traíra, an old Angola mestre usually remembered with Waldemar and Aberrê.

video.description: Songs on this site that include a video recording.

volta-ao-mundo.description: The volta ao mundo is the walk around the circle that pauses the game and starts it again. These songs name that walk.

waldemar.description: Songs that name Mestre Waldemar, also sung as Valdemar, the Angola mestre remembered for his roda and his berimbau.

zumbi.description: Songs that name Zumbi dos Palmares, leader of the great quilombo and a symbol of the fight against slavery.
